## Why this exists

The built-in `/compact` command has two limits that hurt on a slow or unstable
upstream:

- **It refuses instead of queueing.** A manual compaction rejects whenever the
agent is not idle, so

the request is lost in the middle of a running turn.
- **It cannot be stopped from the UI.** The co

mmand request stays open for the
whole summarization run, and the composer ignores submissions while

a command
is in flight. A summarizer that hangs without streaming leaves nothing to
press and nothi

is in flight. A summarizer that hangs without streaming leaves nothing to
press and nothing to type.

This plugin shadows `/compact` with a request that returns immediately, queues
while the agent is bu

sy, and runs the compaction in the background. The
compaction is correlated with the requesting comm

and id, so the Chat transcript
upgrades that command row into the usual compaction card.
## Commands
| command | behavior |

| `/compact` | start now when the agent is idle, otherwise queue until the current turn ends |
| `/c
ompact-cancel` | drop a queued request, abort the running summarizer request, or cancel a compaction
started by another command module |

Both commands reject arguments. `/compact` refuses a second request while one
is queued or running a

## What the transcript shows
The request's own lifecycle row appears immediately:

- `Compaction started in the background.`
- `Compaction queued; it starts when the current turn ends

`Compaction started in the background.`
- `Compaction queued; it starts when the current turn ends.`

Because the requesting command id is passed to the compaction engine as
`sourceCommandId`, the usual

compaction events attach to that row: the
transcript turns it into the standard compaction card onc

e the summary lands.
When the attempt settles, the plugin appends one more `command/done` for the
sa
me id to record the outcome:

- `Compacted 42 history items (~12,345 tokens).`
- `No compactable history yet.`
- `Compaction cance

lled.`
- the documented failure text for `busy`, `changed`, `summary`, `commit` and `persistence`.

The extra `command/done` is deliberate: the command service closes the request
as soon as the handle

r returns (that is what frees the composer), so the only
way to report the background outcome on the

same row is a second lifecycle edge
for that id. Clients fold it into the existing row.
## How it works

- The command registry refuses two global registrations of one name, so the
bundle layer disables th

e built-in `command-compact` row and this plugin
registers its own `/compact` under that name. If a

profile still mounts the
built-in row, the duplicate registration is caught: the plugin logs a warni

ng,
keeps `/compact-cancel` mounted, and leaves the built-in command in place.
- The compaction seam

is not reachable from the profile root: agent presets mount
it inside an isolated per-agent group,

and in practice `agent.ctx` does not
expose it either. The plugin therefore runs whichever `compact`

definition the
agent resolves through `commands.find` — normally the preset-mounted command,
whose

handler closes over the isolated service. That handler runs in the
background with the plugin's own

`AbortSignal`. When no other definition
exists, the plugin falls back to an engine reachable from it

of silently doing nothing.
- Agent presets also register their own scoped `/compact`, which shadows

a
global replacement for those agents. The plugin handles a `/compact` line at
the command service b

oundary, so the queue applies whichever definition the
catalog resolves, and restores the original `

execute` method when the plugin
unloads.
- Cancellation aborts the signal handed to the delegated ha

ndler (or to the
engine directly), which reaches the summarizer request.
- A start that races a newl

y opened turn is retried after
`retryDelayMs`, up to `maxQueueAttempts` times, before the failure is

written
to the row. Queue state is per agent and in memory.
- Nothing runs while the agent is busy:

the queue waits for the agent to go idle
and then starts in maintenance, exactly where the built-in

command would have
run.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` (other releases may differ).
- Node.js `>=20.3`, which provides `Abo

ness `0.2.1-rc.5` (other releases may differ).
- Node.js `>=20.3`, which provides `AbortSignal.any`.
## Limitations

- There is no client-side button. Cancellation is the `/compact-cancel` command;
it works because `/

compact` returns before the summarizer starts.
- The queue lives in memory. A host restart ends the

turn and drops the queued
request; run `/compact` again afterwards.
- Automatic pressure compaction

is untouched; only the manual command is
wrapped. A queued request still compacts if an automatic ru

n already did the
work, because the queue cannot know what the next idle check will find.
- Cancella

tion reporting is immediate, but the final row settles when the
compaction engine returns from the a

borted request.
- Disabling this plugin row while its bundle layer is still enabled leaves no
`/comp

act` at all, because that layer already disabled the built-in command.
Re-enable the `command-compac

t` row in Plugins to get the built-in command
back.
- The command-service interception is a method r

eplacement on the `commands`
service, removed when the plugin unloads. A future harness release that

wraps
or freezes that method would need this approach revisited.
- The fallback cancellation relies

on the session log ending in an unfinished
`compaction/start` marker; a compaction that crashed wit

hout an end marker is
reported as active until the next one completes.
- Delegation depends on the o

ther handler honoring the signal it receives. The
preset-mounted command does, because it passes the

signal straight to the
compaction engine.
